changelog: feat: delete a job from the beta console, and two backend fixes that deleting turned up. DELETE /history/{job_id} runs shutil.rmtree on the results folder AND on the uploaded reads. There is no trash and no undo, and on a machine where the reads were uploaded rather than copied in, that folder is the only copy — so the confirmation says exactly that, in files and megabytes read from the server rather than guessed: 'This removes 214 result files (186.4 MB) and 8 uploaded read files (329.6 MB) from disk... the job cannot be re-run afterwards. There is no undo.' A prompt that only asks 'Are you sure?' is a prompt people click through. The bin in the job list opens that confirmation on the job's own screen rather than deleting in place: a one-click delete on a hover target, in a list people scroll and click to open, is one misclick away from a destroyed result folder. Backend: the delete endpoint refused only 'running'. A QUEUED job has a future waiting on it and a job paused at a checkpoint has a live R process polling for its signal file — deleting either pulls the folder out from under a process about to use it. All three are now refused, with a message saying to cancel first. Clear-all now lists the statuses it is safe to delete instead of excluding the live ones, so a status nobody has thought of yet is kept rather than destroyed. Adds GET /history/{job_id}/usage, which is what lets the prompt state real numbers.
